_comment: `cases` are the P0B-EVAL-GUARD-FIX cases: a single tool result plus the type the FROZEN core
classifies it as, and what the structured-evidence correction layer must do with it. `envelope`
is the runner's real JSON tool-result shape; `result_text` is the Command Code plain-text form.
The test serialises/uses the case verbatim, so nothing here is hand-transformed.
Cases A/B/G are false positives; C/C2/D/E/E2/E3 are real failures that must survive. I was a
conservative residual under P0B-EVAL-GUARD-FIX; under P0B-EVAL-INSPECTION-CONTEXT-FIX it is the
quoted-verdict false positive (a clean read-only inspection owns no verdict) and is REMOVED.
`inspection_context_cases` (CASE-IC-*) are the P0B-EVAL-INSPECTION-CONTEXT-FIX cases: each also
asserts the deterministic operation role and the verdict-ownership outcome. No file name, session
id or exact command is special-cased; the role comes from the command structure alone.
P0B-EVAL-WRAPPER-ROLE-FIX adds `wrapper_role_cases` (CASE-W-A..Y, the brief's A..J plus
timeout-option forms, nested wrappers, unparseable wrappers and execution-dominates-pipe cases)
and `wrapper_failure_cases` (CASE-W-FAIL-1..3: a real unittest/build failure behind a timeout
wrapper and a pipe must SURVIVE even when the top-level exit is 0 or pipeline-advisory).
pipeline_advisory: exit_code 0 here is the status of the last pipeline command (tail/head/cat/...), NOT of the command before the pipe - and the output contains failure indicators. Treat this run as FAILED until proven otherwise: re-run the command WITHOUT the pipe.
